name: fast-project-start
body:
`apg project start` must be near-instant when the main checkout's scan is current for main's HEAD. After the unchanged refusals (in-worktree, unborn/detached main, version gate, dirty main), start checks whether the main checkout's scan is fresh for main's HEAD (`git::is_fresh` over the main layout root) — the guard must be `!is_fresh`, because `git::is_stale` alone returns false when no `db.lbug`/`graph.jsonl` exists, so it cannot detect a missing scan. When the scan is stale or missing, start REFUSES with guidance to run `apg scan` in the main checkout first. When the scan is fresh, start creates the branch + worktree (off the default branch, unchanged) and copies the main checkout's `apg/.trans` artifacts into the new worktree's `apg/.trans` — no scan, no frontend spawns. This is correct without re-assembly because the graph stores repo-relative paths (`path`/File FQN are repo-relative, not worktree-absolute), so main's DB is valid verbatim in the worktree; the worktree's tree equals main's HEAD, so the recorded content identity still matches.

Acceptance criteria:
- Starting a project when main's scan is stale or missing refuses, and the refusal tells the user to run `apg scan` in the main checkout.
- Starting a project when main's scan is fresh for main's HEAD spawns no frontend process.
- The resulting branch DB contains the same code nodes and edges as a full scan of main's HEAD under the same effective scan configuration (the blacklist is not part of the cache key, so a recorded config mismatch is undetectable from the store — see `requirements.note.blacklist-not-in-cache-key`).
- The copy completes without a full-tree walk of the source files.
- Correctness is preserved because main's scan is valid verbatim in the new worktree (repo-relative paths; the worktree's tree equals main's HEAD).
